alex: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernel RFC — we need to lock the interface and a rollout plan for Triton vs CUTLASS. High level: Triton = faster iteration and easier custom ops, CUTLASS/CUDA = more battle-tested perf and memory predictability. Need explicit contracts, fallback rules, and test coverage. Who can own which pieces?

maria: I ran microbenchmarks on A100 (32G) with our eval harness. Results quick summary: Triton beats CUTLASS ~12% for seq<=512 on throughput, but at seq=2048 we saw memory spikes and a few OOMs. CUTLASS gave slightly lower peak throughput but stable memory. Raw: Triton 780 tks/s (512), 210 tks/s (2048, intermittent OOM); CUTLASS 695 tks/s (512), 200 tks/s (2048, stable).

jordan: Agree on adapter layer. Main risk is KV-cache ABI/layout differences. Propose a minimal kernel-adapter contract: allocate_kv(device_ptr, batch, heads, head_dim), step_attention(kv_handle, q_ptr, k_ptr, v_ptr, out_ptr, seq_len, causal_flag). That keeps runtime decoupled from kernel implementation.

kevin: +1. Also recommend a kernel registry with metadata so routing/selection can be automated. Fields: arch (tensorrt/triton/cutlass), seq_range (<=512,512-2048,>2048), quant (fp16/int8), deterministic=true/false. Example metadata tag: `cutlass::seq:512-2048::fp16::deterministic`.

priya: I'll own the rollout/checklist. Proposal: canary -> small internal traffic -> perf validation -> wider rollout. Canary gating rules: no OOMs, p95 latency within 1.15x baseline, token-cost delta < 5%. Timeline: prepare artifacts this week, canary next Tue. Owners: Priya (rollout), Kevin (ci + registry), Jordan (adapter RFC), Maria (bench harness & perf set).

lia: Need dashboards and alerts before canary: p50/p95 token latency, OOM count, GPU mem_used, KV-cache occupancy, model-output QA regression. Add canary label to metrics. Also include automatic fallback metric that forces previous kernel if anomalies spike.

sre-bot: Scheduled deploy event created: canary-attn-kernel 1758001400 -> target=redwood-internal. Alerts channel=#eng-oncall.

alex: Summarizing action items: 1) Kernel adapter RFC PR (owner: jordan) - due Fri EOD. 2) Kernel registry proto + schema (owner: kevin) - due Mon. 3) Expand bench harness + standard prompt set + deterministic seed (owner: maria) - due Wed. 4) Canary playbook + dashboards + alerts (owners: priya/lia) - canary next Tue. 5) Fallback policy doc (owner: alex) - draft by next Wed.

maria: small implementation note: add a deterministic flag for FP16 kernels and a seeded eval path so we can reproduce regressions. Also include a mode that disables autotune to compare baseline vs tuned kernels.

kevin: I'll sketch the registry proto and push an empty repo + CI template today. Will include selector pseudocode: ```python
# choose kernel by runtime selectors
def choose_kernel(model, seq_len, quant, stability_require):
    candidates = registry.lookup(model.arch)
    filter_by_seq = [c for c in candidates if c.seq_min<=seq_len<=c.seq_max]
    filter_by_quant = [c for c in filter_by_seq if c.quant==quant]
    sort_by = lambda c: (c.stability_score if stability_require else -c.throughput)
    return sorted(filter_by_quant, key=sort_by)[0]
```

priya: I'll create the canary playbook doc and link it once ready. We should include exact traffic percentages and rollback triggers (p95 > 1.15x for >5min OR any OOMs).

alex: One more cross-cutting concern: licensing and kernel distribution for private deployments. Kevin — note that CUTLASS-derived kernels might have different redistribution constraints than Triton packages. Add a license field to registry metadata.

lia: Noted. Also add a consumer-facing flag in the control plane so customers can pin to kernel families (e.g., "cutlass-stable" vs "triton-experimental").

jordan: I'll open the adapter RFC and include ABI examples and a tiny reference implementation that wraps both Triton and CUTLASS backends. Will include unit tests that validate KV layout invariants.

maria: I'll add the standard prompt set and a small regression harness that runs deterministic seed across both kernels and writes per-token diffs.

kevin: repo created: github.com/redwood-inference/kernel-registry (placeholder). CI template will validate metadata schema and run a sanity harness.

priya: Thanks all — I put the canary date in my calendar and will ping again when playbook draft is ready. @alex I'll need the fallback policy draft to include exact SLO numbers to wire alerts.

alex: Will do. Thanks everyone — next check-in on this thread after Jordan's RFC is up. :thumbsup:
